title: 3. Major Natural Vegetation Types of the World

blocks.content: Global vegetation zones are closely linked with climatic belts.
Natural vegetation refers to a plant community that has grown naturally without human aid and has been left undisturbed by humans for a long time.

rows: No uniform leaf-shedding season; remains green year-round
Sheds leaves for 6-8 weeks during dry summer
Amazon Basin, Congo Basin, Southeast Asia
India, Myanmar, Central America, Northern Australia

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tropical Evergreen Forests thrive in equatorial regions with high annual rainfall, dense multi-layered canopies, and rich biodiversity.
Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon) Forests shed leaves during the dry season to minimize transpiration loss.
Mediterranean Vegetation features broad-leaved sclerophyllous plants adapted to hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters.
Coniferous Boreal (Taiga) Forests consist predominantly of softwood trees such as pine, spruce, and fir in sub-arctic regions.
Tundra Vegetation is restricted to extreme polar environments dominated by mosses, lichens, and dwarf shrubs.
The Mediterranean region is heavily tested for its specialization in citrus fruits, orchard farming, and viticulture.
Temperate grassland nomenclature is a recurring question: Prairies (North America), Pampas (South America), Steppes (Eurasia), Velds (South Africa), and Downs (Australia).
The Amazonian rainforests (Selvas) are frequently cited as the 'Lungs of the Earth' due to their planetary oxygen contribution.

cells: Dense multi-layered forests; hardwood trees; extremely high biodiversity.
Trees shed leaves to conserve water; teak and sal common.
Tall grasses with scattered trees; supports large herbivores.
Sparse xerophytic plants; thick cuticle and long roots.
